title: Motion
objective: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to describe motion using distance and time, calculate speed with speed = distance / time, and give the answer with the right units.

sections.title: Distance
sections.text: Distance is how far something travels. It is measured in metres (m) or, for longer journeys, kilometres (km). A runner who goes once around a 400 m track has travelled 400 m.

sections.title: Time
sections.text: Time is how long the journey takes. It is measured in seconds (s), minutes or hours (h). In a race, a stopwatch measures the time from the start to the finish line.

sections.title: Speed = distance / time
sections.text: Speed tells you how fast something moves. To find it, divide the distance by the time. A runner who covers 100 m in 20 s has a speed of 100 / 20 = 5 metres per second (m/s). The units of speed come from both units, so speed can be in m/s or km/h.

sections.title: Comparing speeds
sections.text: To compare speeds, use the same units. A bus in Nairobi travelling at 60 km/h would cover 60 km in one hour. A cheetah can sprint at about 100 km/h, but only for a short time. If two people walk the same distance, the one who takes less time is faster.

examples.title: Example 1: The speed of a runner
examples.code:
distance = 100
time = 20
speed = distance / time
print(speed, "m/s")

examples.title: Example 2: How far does a bus go?
examples.code:
speed = 60
hours = 2
distance = speed * hours
print(distance, "km")

check_questions.prompt: A cyclist rides 30 km in 2 hours. What is the cyclist's average speed?

misconception.0: That multiplies distance by time. Speed is distance divided by time.
misconception.1: That adds the numbers. Speed is distance divided by time.
misconception.3: That subtracts the numbers. Speed is distance divided by time.

check_questions.prompt: Which of these is a unit of speed?
check_questions.explanation: Speed is distance divided by time, so its unit is a distance unit per time unit, such as m/s.

check_questions.prompt: Kofi and Ada walk the same route to the market. Kofi takes 10 minutes and Ada takes 15 minutes. Who walked faster?
options: Ada, because she walked for longer
They walked at the same speed
check_questions.explanation: They covered the same distance, and Kofi took less time, so Kofi was faster.

misconception.0: Taking longer for the same distance means a slower speed.
misconception.2: Same distance in different times means different speeds.
misconception.3: You can compare them because the distance is the same.

try_it.title: Try It Yourself
try_it.instructions: Time how long it takes you to walk 10 metres. Change distance and time to your numbers and run the code to find your speed in m/s.

time = 20
